resources.string: Noun (ism)
A word for a person, thing, place or idea that is not tied to a time: رَبّ, ٱلْكِتَاب, هُوَ.
Verb (fiʿl)
A word for an action or happening tied to a time: past, present or future: قَالَ, يَعْلَمُ.
Particle (ḥarf)
A word that only has its full meaning with other words: فِي \"in\", مِنْ \"from\", وَ \"and\".
Masculine and feminine (mudhakkar, muʾannath)
Every noun is masculine or feminine. Most feminine nouns end in ة, as in رَحْمَة.
The dual (muthannā)
Two of something, made by adding ـَانِ or ـَيْنِ: جَنَّتَانِ \"two gardens\".
Sound masculine plural
A plural of men made by adding ـُونَ or ـِينَ to the unchanged singular: مُؤْمِنُونَ.
Sound feminine plural
A plural made by adding ـَات to the singular: مُؤْمِنَات, سَمَٰوَٰت.
Broken plural (jamʿ taksīr)
A plural made by reshaping the word itself, with no fixed ending: رَجُل becomes رِجَال.
Definite and indefinite (maʿrifa, nakira)
A definite noun is a particular one (\"the book\"); an indefinite noun is any one (\"a book\"), usually with tanwīn.
The three cases (rafʿ, naṣb, jarr)
A noun’s ending shows its job in the sentence: ḍamma for rafʿ, fatḥa for naṣb, kasra for jarr.
Dual and plural endings
Duals and sound masculine plurals show the case with letters instead: ـَانِ / ـَيْنِ and ـُونَ / ـِينَ.
Partly declining nouns (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf)
Some nouns never take tanwīn, and take a fatḥa where others take a kasra: إِبْرَٰهِيمَ.
The five nouns (al-asmāʾ al-khamsa)
أَب, أَخ, حَم, فُو and ذُو show their case with a long vowel when they are followed by another word: أَبُوهُ, أَبَاهُ, أَبِيهِ.
Detached pronouns (ḍamīr munfaṣil)
Pronouns that stand on their own: هُوَ \"he\", أَنْتُمْ \"you all\", نَحْنُ \"we\". Every pronoun is definite.
Attached pronouns (ḍamīr muttaṣil)
Pronouns joined to the end of a word: رَبُّكَ \"your Lord\", عَلَيْهِمْ \"on them\", خَلَقَنَا \"created us\".
إِيَّا, the pronoun base for objects
إِيَّا carries an attached pronoun so an object can come first: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ \"You alone we worship\".
This and that (ism ishāra)
Words that point: هَٰذَا \"this\", ذَٰلِكَ \"that\", هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ \"these\", أُولَٰٓئِكَ \"those\".
Who and which (ism mawṣūl)
Words meaning \"the one who\" or \"that which\", completed by the clause after them: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا, مَا.
Preposition and its noun (ḥarf jarr)
A preposition such as فِي, مِنْ, عَلَىٰ or بِـ puts the noun after it in jarr: فِي ٱلْأَرْضِ.
Possessive phrase (iḍāfa)
Two nouns joined as \"X of Y\": the first (muḍāf) loses ال and tanwīn, the second (muḍāf ilayh) is always in jarr: رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ.
A pronoun as the possessor
An attached pronoun can be the second part of an iḍāfa: رَبُّكَ \"your Lord\", كِتَٰبُهُ \"his book\".
Adjective and agreement (naʿt)
An adjective comes after its noun and matches it in case, definiteness, number and gender: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ.
Comparative and superlative (ism al-tafḍīl)
The pattern أَفْعَل means \"more\" or \"most\": أَكْبَرُ \"greater, greatest\", أَعْلَمُ \"knows best\".
Subject and predicate (mubtadaʾ, khabar)
A nominal sentence opens with what it talks about (mubtadaʾ) and then says something about it (khabar), both in rafʿ: ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ.
A predicate that is a phrase or a sentence
The khabar can be a preposition phrase (ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ) or a whole sentence (ٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ).
The predicate placed first
When the subject is indefinite and the khabar is a phrase, the khabar comes first: لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ \"for them is a punishment\".
The three-letter root
Most words are built on three root letters carrying a core meaning: ك ت ب \"writing\" in كَتَبَ, كِتَٰب, مَكْتُوب.
Patterns on the scale فَعَلَ (wazn)
Words are shaped by patterns measured with ف ع ل: كَاتِب is on فَاعِل \"one who does\", مَكْتُوب on مَفْعُول \"one done to\".
Past-tense verb (al-māḍī)
A finished action. Endings show who did it: فَعَلْتُ \"I did\", فَعَلُوا \"they did\".
The doer inside the verb
The ending of a verb can itself be the doer: in ءَامَنُوا the و is \"they\", the ones who believed.
Present/future verb (al-muḍāriʿ)
An action now or to come, with a prefix for who does it: يَعْلَمُ \"he knows\", نَعْبُدُ \"we worship\".
Subjunctive after أَنْ and لَنْ
After أَنْ, لَنْ, كَيْ and حَتَّىٰ a present verb is in naṣb: لَنْ تَنَالُوا \"you will never attain\".
Jussive after لَمْ and in conditions
After لَمْ, لَا of forbidding and in conditions a present verb is in jazm, shown by a sukūn or a dropped letter: لَمْ يَلِدْ.
قَدْ, سَـ and سَوْفَ
قَدْ before a past verb means \"has indeed\"; سَـ and سَوْفَ before a present verb mean \"will\".
Imperative verb (al-amr)
A command to the one addressed: قُلْ \"say\", ٱعْبُدُوا \"worship\".
Forbidding with لَا
لَا before a present verb in jazm means \"do not\": لَا تَحْزَنْ \"do not grieve\".
Passive voice
The doer is left out and something else takes its place: خُلِقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ \"man was created\".
Inna and its sisters
إِنَّ, أَنَّ, لَكِنَّ, كَأَنَّ, لَعَلَّ and لَيْتَ come before a nominal sentence and put its subject in naṣb: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ.
Kāna and its sisters
كَانَ, أَصْبَحَ, لَيْسَ and their sisters come before a nominal sentence and put its predicate in naṣb: كَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا.
لَا denying a whole kind
لَا before an indefinite noun with a fatḥa and no tanwīn denies every one of its kind: لَا رَيْبَ \"no doubt at all\".
Verb, doer and object
A verbal sentence opens with a verb; its doer (fāʿil) is in rafʿ and what it acts on (mafʿūl bihi) in naṣb: خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ.
Verb agreement
A verb before its doer stays singular but matches its gender; a verb after its doer matches it in number too.
The hidden doer
When no doer is written, it is understood from the verb: يَعْلَمُ \"he knows\", with \"he\" hidden inside.
Verb forms II–IV
Extra letters change a root’s meaning: فَعَّلَ (II) often \"make do\", فَاعَلَ (III) \"do with someone\", أَفْعَلَ (IV) \"cause\".
Verb forms V–VI
تَفَعَّلَ (V) and تَفَاعَلَ (VI) add تَـ, often meaning \"do to oneself\" or \"do to each other\": تَسَآءَلُونَ.
Verb forms VII–X
ٱنْفَعَلَ (VII), ٱفْتَعَلَ (VIII), ٱفْعَلَّ (IX) and ٱسْتَفْعَلَ (X), such as ٱسْتَعَانَ \"seek help\".
Hollow verbs, such as قَالَ
Verbs with و or ي in the middle of the root, which turns into a long vowel or drops: قَالَ, يَقُولُ, قُلْ.
Defective verbs, such as هَدَىٰ
Verbs with و or ي at the end of the root, which changes or drops: هَدَىٰ, يَهْدِي, لَمْ يَهْدِ.
Assimilated, doubled and hamzated verbs
Roots starting with و (وَعَدَ, يَعِدُ), with the same last two letters (رَدَّ) or with a hamza (أَخَذَ).
The doer noun (ism al-fāʿil)
A noun for the one who does the action, on فَاعِل or with مُـ in the longer forms: كَافِر, مُؤْمِن.
The done-to noun (ism al-mafʿūl)
A noun for the one the action is done to, on مَفْعُول or مُـ…َـ: مَغْضُوب, مُسْتَقِيم.
The verbal noun (maṣdar)
The name of the action itself, like \"-ing\": ٱلْحَمْد \"praising\", عِبَادَة \"worshipping\".
Nouns of place, time and intensity
مَفْعَل for where or when (مَسْجِد \"place of prostration\") and patterns like فَعَّال or فَعِيل for \"very\" (غَفَّار, رَحِيم).
Absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq)
A verbal noun in naṣb from the same verb, to stress it or say how or how often: وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكْلِيمًا.
Object of reason (mafʿūl lahu)
A verbal noun in naṣb that says why the action happened: حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ \"for fear of death\".
Object of time or place (ẓarf)
A word in naṣb for when or where the action happened: يَوْمَ, بَيْنَ, عِنْدَ.
Circumstance (ḥāl)
A word in naṣb describing the state someone was in as the action happened: يَدْخُلُونَ … أَفْوَاجًا \"entering in crowds\".
Specifier (tamyīz)
An indefinite noun in naṣb that makes clear what a number or vague word is about: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا \"eleven stars\".
Conditions with إِنْ, مَنْ and إِذَا
\"If … then …\": إِنْ, مَنْ and مَا put both verbs in jazm; إِذَا is \"when\", about something sure to come.
لَوْ and لَوْلَا
لَوْ \"if only, had it been\" for what did not happen; لَوْلَا \"were it not for\".
Questions (istifhām)
أَ and هَلْ ask yes-or-no; مَنْ \"who\", مَا \"what\", كَيْفَ \"how\", أَيْنَ \"where\" ask for more.
Exception with إِلَّا
إِلَّا takes a word out of what was said, and that word (mustathnā) is usually in naṣb: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ.
Calling with يَا and يَٰٓأَيُّهَا
يَا calls someone; before a noun with ال it becomes يَٰٓأَيُّهَا: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ.
وَ, فَـ and ثُمَّ
وَ joins \"and\", فَـ \"and so, then at once\", ثُمَّ \"then, after a while\". What follows matches what it joins.
The uses of مَا
مَا can ask \"what?\", mean \"that which\", or deny \"not\": مَا هُمْ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ.
The uses of لَا
لَا denies \"no, not\", forbids \"do not\", or denies a whole kind: لَا رَيْبَ.
Four look-alikes: إِنْ \"if\" or \"not\", أَنْ \"to, that\" before a verb, إِنَّ \"indeed\", أَنَّ \"that\" before a noun.
The lām particles
لِـ \"for, belonging to\", لَـ \"surely\", and لِـ of purpose or command before a verb: لِيَعْبُدُونِ.
Emphasis and oaths
إِنَّ, لَـ and the doubled نّ strengthen a statement; وَ in an oath means \"by\": وَٱلْعَصْرِ.
Restriction and word order
Putting a word first, or مَا … إِلَّا and إِنَّمَا, means \"only\": إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ \"You alone we worship\".
